candidate.answerReason: Four tires are used during every mile, giving 120,000 miles of combined tire use. Dividing equally among five tires gives 24,000 miles each.

methods.label: Share the combined tire use
methods.explanation:
For every mile the car travels, four tires are each used for one mile. Thus, during the first \(30{,}000\) miles, the combined use of all the tires is
\[
4\cdot30{,}000=120{,}000\text{ miles}.
\]
Since the five tires share this use equally, each tire is used for
\[
120{,}000\div5=24{,}000\text{ miles}.
\]
The answer is \(24{,}000\) miles, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary multiplication and equal sharing, within AMC 8 scope.

candidate.annotationRationale: Equal sharing of the combined tire mileage is the division application assessed by cnm_p084. The written method uses cnm_p111 to organize the total usage relationship, supported by the equal-addends meaning of multiplication in cnm_p038.
